html:
The war between the United States and eleven Southern states that broke away to form the Confederate States of America, fought from 1861 to 1865. It ended with the defeat of the South and the end of slavery in the country.

The root cause was slavery and whether it would spread to the West. After Abraham Lincoln was elected president in 1860, Southern states seceded. The war began when Confederates fired on Fort Sumter in April 1861.

The main turns:

  • 1862: the Union stopped a Southern invasion at Antietam.
  • 1 January 1863: Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation declared the enslaved in rebel areas free; about 180,000 Black soldiers then served the Union.
  • July 1863: Union victories at Gettysburg and Vicksburg.
  • 1864: Union armies marched through Georgia, destroying farms and railroads.
  • April 1865: Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant, and days later Lincoln was murdered.

Some 620,000 to 750,000 soldiers died, more than in any other American war. The Thirteenth Amendment abolished slavery in December 1865. The Union blockade of Southern cotton also boosted cotton growing in Egypt and India, as with Egyptian cotton.
sum: The war between the United States and eleven Southern states that broke away to form the Confederate States of America, fought from 1861 to 1865. It ended with the defeat of the South and the end of slavery in the country.
